item.title: Press Coverage: Sonny Styles and Arvell Reese Wow at NFL Scouting Combine, Buckeyes Rave About Coordinators and Returning Players
item.description: What an incredible evening Thursday was for Sonny Styles. The former Ohio State linebacker posted some of the best numbers in the history of the linebacker position at the NFL Scouting Combine, posting a 43.5-inch vertical leap, 11-foot-2 broad jump and 4.46-second 40-yard dash, all of which led linebackers at the combine. item.description: “Who’s the best receiver in this draft class?” That was the question floated to former Ohio State wide receiver Carnell Tate at the NFL Scouting Combine on Friday. item.title: Lorenzo Styles Jr. Runs 4.27-Second 40-Yard Dash, Fastest Time Ever For A Buckeye at the NFL Scouting Combine
item.description: Lorenzo Styles Jr. is the fastest Buckeye in NFL Scouting Combine history. The former Ohio State defensive back ran a 4.27-second 40-yard dash at Lucas Oil Stadium on Friday, becoming the first-ever Buckeye to break 4.3 seconds in the 40 at the combine. Styles broke the previous record of 4.31 seconds, run by both Curtis Samuel (2017) and Parris Campbell (2019), for the fastest 40 time by a former Ohio State player since the combine began releasing official times. item.description: Sonny Styles and Lorenzo Styles Jr. have generated headlines at the NFL Scouting Combine this week. item.title: Ohio State Breaks Single-Game Record With 18 3-Pointers in 87-68 Road Win Over No. 15 Michigan State
item.description: Ohio State women’s basketball finished its regular season with a record-breaking performance against a top-15 team. The Buckeyes broke their single-game school record for 3-pointers in a game as Ohio State made 18 of 32 3-point shot attempts on their way to a 87-68 win over No. 15 Michigan State in East Lansing. item.title: Massive 82-74 Upset Win Over No. 8 Purdue Revives Ohio State in NCAA Tournament Race
item.description: For roughly the 10,000th time this season, when it seemed Ohio State's NCAA Tournament hopes were on life support, the Buckeyes took themselves from a great valley to a mountaintop. Coming off perhaps its worst performance of the season at Iowa, Ohio State banded together behind a scorching outing from John Mobley Jr. and stunned No. 8 Purdue (22-7, 12-7 Big Ten) in the Schottenstein Center in an 80-71 win.
